name: Barbería Continental FL
niche: barberia boutique (barbershop, Latin-owned, fades + beard work)
address_note: Booksy and Fresha both list the street as 'Daytona Beach, FL 32117'; some older aggregator snippets (Yelp listing title, one BestProsInTown mention) tag the city as 'Holly Hill, FL' instead. Same building either way (675 Mason Ave sits right on the Daytona Beach / Holly Hill line). Geo-coordinates from Booksy (29.22356, -81.03747) and Fresha (29.223585, -81.037498) match almost exactly, both resolve on Google Maps to Daytona Beach addressing, so the site uses Daytona Beach, FL per the task brief and per the two live booking-platform listings.
phone_source: CORRECTED from the task brief's starting number. (386) 293-4825 (the number given at the start of this task) independently resolves, via two separate web searches, to the SIBLING shop 'Barbería Flow Latino' at the SAME address (675 Mason Ave) and same booking-platform family, not to Barbería Continental FL itself. The number actually published for Barbería Continental FL, (386) 333-1712, is confirmed by THREE independent sources: (1) a Yelp business-listing search snippet naming 'Barberia Continental' specifically, (2) Fresha's own page JSON data for this exact listing (telephone:+1 386-333-1712, contactNumber:+1 386-333-1712, found via curl on the live Fresha page), and (3) the business's own self-published digital contact card at dot.cards/barbercontinental (phone_items -> value 3863331712, labeled 'contactanos', SMS-enabled) which also links out to this business's own Instagram and Facebook. Booksy's own JSON-LD does not publish a phone field for this listing (phone: null in the raw dossier).
rating_source: Fetched directly from the live Booksy business page JSON-LD (booksy.com/en-us/1579021_barberia-continental-fl_barber-shop_16100_daytona-beach) via scripts/booksy_dossier.py: aggregateRating ratingValue 4.809523809523809 (rounds to 4.8), reviewCount 21. This matches the number given in the task brief exactly and is the most authoritative reachable source (Booksy is the primary booking platform and the live page is directly fetchable, unlike Google Maps which is JS-rendered). A separate cached web-search snippet surfaced an older '5.0 x 16 reviews' figure for the same Booksy listing; that is treated as a stale index snapshot from before the listing accrued more reviews, not the current number. Fresha shows 0 reviews for this listing (booking not yet active there), consistent with Booksy being the primary/active platform.
staff_source: Listed as the sole employee/staff member in the Booksy JSON-LD (employee[].name). Corroborated by a review ('William is awesome, good barber and very meticulous') and by a real photo (bk-6, not used on the final site due to text overlay) showing a discount card held up that reads 'BARBERIA CONTINENTAL ... BARBERO: WILLIAMS'.
hours_source: Live Booksy JSON-LD openingHoursSpecification (Tue-Fri 11:15-18:00, Sat 11:15-16:30, closed Sun/Mon), pulled directly from the actual booking calendar so treated as authoritative. Fresha's page separately lists a generic 'Mon-Sat 10:00-18:00' block, but Fresha also states this venue is 'currently not accepting online bookings through Fresha', so its hours read as an unmaintained default rather than the real schedule. Booksy hours used on the site.
walk_ins_note: No explicit 'walk-ins welcome' statement found on any source; booking is Booksy-first (real online calendar with specific 15-minute slot starts, e.g. 11:15), so the site's booking CTA points to Booksy rather than claiming walk-in availability that was not verified.
booking_platform: Booksy (primary, live calendar, real prices/durations) + Fresha (secondary listing, present but bookings not active there)
ig_note: Direct WebFetch and direct curl of instagram.com/barberiacontinentalfl/ and the web_profile_info API both returned HTTP 429 (rate limited) on every attempt made during this research pass. Photos were still obtained successfully through the project's dedicated IG photo microservice (scripts/ig_photos.py, Railway-hosted, different egress path), which returned 12 real posts. Bio text / external link / follower count could not be read (no working channel reached them this session); not fabricated.
facebook_note: Resolved from the Booksy sameAs share-link and independently from a second share-link on the business's own dot.cards profile (both redirect to the same Facebook page ID 61582479897956, 'Barberia Continental FL'). WebFetch of the resolved page URL returned only a truncated shell (Facebook's anti-scraping wall), so no About-section text or extra contact info could be read from it.
own_contact_card_note: Self-published digital business-card page (dot.cards), evidently set up by the owner: phone (contactanos / SMS-enabled, matches the corrected phone above), a Google Maps link to this exact address, links out to this business's own Instagram and Facebook, and the source of the real circular logo image (see photos_source). No email field is present on this card.

language_note: Judgment call documented honestly: signals point in both directions. FOR Spanish as primary: business name uses the Spanish spelling 'Barbería', explicitly Latin-owned per multiple aggregator descriptions, sibling shop at the same address is literally named 'Flow LATINO', and the owner's own self-published dot.cards contact page uses Spanish button labels ('contactanos', 'direccion', 'AGENDA TU CITA'). FOR English as primary: the actual review text pulled from the live Booksy page is overwhelmingly English (9 of 10 sampled reviews, including all 3 fully-verified named ones: 'Best in the area', 'Great cut every time.', 'Nice haircut'; only 1 of 10 is Spanish), and Booksy's own language heuristic over that review corpus also lands on 'en'. Went with English as the DEFAULT language (matches the data-driven review-corpus signal, which is the most direct evidence of how actual customers in Daytona Beach engage with this business) while building the site fully bilingual with a prominent ES/EN toggle, since the Latin-owned identity and Spanish-speaking share of the clientele are real and well documented.

reviews_note: Author names shown as 'Gabriel M...', 'Logan S...', 'Fernando R...' because Booksy itself publishes reviewer names in this truncated first-name + last-initial format (privacy feature of the platform); this is the real, verbatim public format, not a redaction we introduced. Only the 3 reviews with a verified author+quote pairing from the JSON-LD are used as testimonials on the site.
brand_vibe: Boutique barbershop interior with deep red/maroon walls and gold vintage-style barber chairs (visible in every real photo), matched by the business's own official circular logo (downloaded from the owner's dot.cards contact page): a mustard-gold background with black line art of a bearded barber, wordmark 'BARBERIA CONTINENTAL FL'. Built on dark-v2 with hue shifted to a deeper, richer brass/copper-gold (44) at higher saturation and lower lightness than the base template's flat gold and than nearby-hued barbershop demos already in the portfolio (domes-barber-studio-pompano hue 21, natdenmarkbarber hue 32, palm-beach-barber-studio hue 15), so the palette stays true to the real logo color family while reading as its own distinct, richer tone rather than a repeat of the base template gold.
photos_source: scripts/booksy_dossier.py -> scripts/booksy_gallery.py pulled 6 photos from Booksy first; scripts/ig_photos.py (Railway IG photo service) against @barberiacontinentalfl then returned 12 real Instagram posts, which overwrote the Booksy set in assets/raw (same bk-N naming) and were used as the final photo set since they had more volume and variety. All 12 verified as real, valid JPEGs over 15KB with `file`. Visually curated one by one via the contact sheet (output/barberia-continental-daytona/_sheet.jpg): 9 of 12 kept (bk-1, bk-2, bk-3, bk-4, bk-5, bk-9, bk-10, bk-11, bk-12), 3 discarded (bk-6: real barbershop scene but a business/discount card with text is held up covering part of the frame, text-overlay rule; bk-7 and bk-8: Snapchat-filter selfies with a text mask over the face, not usable per the no-selfies-as-tiles rule and not clean enough even for a small avatar). bk-5 was a vertical video frame with black letterbox bars top and bottom (a braid/cornrow design shot); cropped with PIL to remove the black bars, keeping only the real photo content, since it shows a specialty (braid/design work) not otherwise represented. The official logo (downloaded from the owner's own dot.cards contact page, Firebase-hosted, 1024x1024, resized to 800px/quality 85 for performance) is used as the brand mark, avatar and JSON-LD icon instead of reusing a client photo, since a real dedicated logo exists for this business (unlike most demos in this pipeline).
